subject: general
question: What maximum sustained wind speed range was forecast for Cyclone Montha before landfall in October 2025?
solution:
p data-end="57" data-start="0">The correct answer is __**90-100 km/h**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Cyclone Montha** was a tropical cyclone that developed in the **North Indian Ocean** basin, specifically in the **Bay of Bengal**, during **October 2025**.
 
• The **India Meteorological Department (IMD)** issued bulletins forecasting that the system would maintain a **maximum sustained wind speed** in the range of **90-100 km/h** just before making landfall.
 
• With wind speeds reaching **90-100 km/h**, the system was classified as a **Severe Cyclonic Storm**. This category typically involves wind speeds between **89 km/h and 117 km/h**. ***Hence, the statement regarding the 90-100 km/h range is correct.***
 
• The forecast also indicated **gusting** speeds reaching up to **110 km/h**, which posed a significant threat to temporary structures and agricultural crops in the **coastal districts**.
 
• The landfall was projected to impact the **eastern coast of India**, specifically affecting the states of **Odisha** and **West Bengal**, leading to the mobilization of **NDRF (National Disaster Response Force)** teams.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Classification of Cyclones:**
 
 
• The **IMD** classifies cyclonic disturbances based on their **maximum sustained surface wind speed (MSW)**. A **Cyclonic Storm** has speeds of **62-88 km/h**, while a **Severe Cyclonic Storm** ranges from **89-117 km/h**.
 
• If the winds exceed **118-165 km/h**, it is termed a **Very Severe Cyclonic Storm**, and anything above **221 km/h** is a **Super Cyclonic Storm**.
 
 
 
• **Sustained Wind Speed:**
 
 
• In the context of Indian meteorology, **sustained wind speed** is usually measured as a **3-minute average** or a **10-minute average** at a height of **10 meters**.
 
• This metric is crucial for determining the **potential damage** to infrastructure and the height of the **storm surge** expected during landfall.
 
 
 
• **Cyclone Naming:**
 
 
• The name **Montha** was contributed by **Myanmar** as part of the naming protocol established by the **WMO/ESCAP** Panel on Tropical Cyclones.
 
• Naming helps in **disaster risk communication** and avoids confusion when multiple systems are active simultaneously in the same **geographical region**.
 
 
 
• **Impact and Mitigation:**
 
 
• A wind range of **90-100 km/h** is strong enough to cause the **uprooting of trees**, damage to **power lines**, and significant **storm surges** of about **0.5 to 1.0 meter** above the astronomical tide.
 
• The **Integrated Cyclone Adventure System** and **satellite imagery** (such as **INSAT-3DR**) are used to track the **latitude** and **longitude** of the eye of the storm.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Historical Context:** **October** and **November** are considered the peak **post-monsoon cyclone season** for the **Bay of Bengal** due to high **sea surface temperatures**.
 
• **Landfall Characteristics:** The **landfall** process involves the center of the **cyclone eye** moving over the coast, where the highest **wind pressure** is often felt in the **right forward quadrant** of the storm.
 
• **Warning Protocols:** The **IMD** uses a **four-stage warning system**: **Pre-Cyclone Watch**, **Cyclone Alert** (Yellow), **Cyclone Warning** (Orange), and **Post-Landfall Outlook** (Red).
